t: Minimum Moves to Convert String: Greedy Leftmost-X Anchoring
o:
**Understanding the problem**

One move converts any three consecutive characters to 'O' (cells already holding 'O' simply stay); find the fewest moves that eliminate every 'X'. "XXX" clears in one move covering all three cells. "XXOX" needs two — first stamp positions 0-2, then cover the trailing X with a window over the last three characters; windows may overlap. "OOOO" already has no X, so zero moves suffice. Any single move can only help if it erases at least one remaining X, and the leftmost uncovered X forces a window anchored near it; n is at most 1000, so the challenge is proving minimality rather than raw speed.
k: Exchange argument for greedy optimality: the leftmost uncovered X must lie in some chosen window, and sliding that window left until it starts exactly there never destroys coverage.
When the leftmost X sits at index i, one move handles i, i+1, i+2 at once, so scanning may resume at i+3.
Equivalently, each maximal block of X of length L costs ceil(L/3) moves, since blocks do not interact.

a.n: Approach 1: Greedy Scan with Three-Cell Jumps
a.i: Scan left to right. On meeting an X at index i, spend one move anchored there — it covers i through i+2 regardless of what those cells hold — and jump to i+3; on O, advance one cell. Delaying each move until forced anchors every window at an actual X, which the exchange argument shows is minimal.
s: While i < n: if s[i] is X, increment moves and set i += 3.
a.t: O(n) — every index is visited once by the advancing pointer.

a.n: Approach 2: Ceiling Division per Maximal X-Block
a.i: Split the string into maximal runs of consecutive X separated by O's; a run of length L needs ceil(L/3) windows, and distinct runs are independent. Accumulating (L + 2) / 3 per run yields the same total without simulating jumps and makes the structure explicit — for the sample XXOX, runs of lengths 2 and 1 give 1 + 1 = 2.
s: Iterate characters keeping the length of the current X-run.
On hitting O, add (run + 2) / 3 to the answer and reset run to zero.
After the loop, flush any trailing run with (run + 2) / 3.
a.t: O(n) — a single pass over the string.

w:
**Takeaway**

Greedy leftmost-X anchoring is the interview answer; state the exchange argument to justify optimality. Pitfalls: the final greedy window may conceptually overrun the end of the string — in reality slide it left to cover the tail block, and the count is unchanged; also remember overlapping windows are allowed. Follow-ups: minimum moves with stamps of general length k, or weighted conversion costs per position.
